FIRST DCA-specific evaluation (new methodology this run: run_dca_backtest has no round-trip trades, so PF/trade-count bar does not apply -- instead compared capital-normalized ROI (unrealized_pnl/invested %) of the SHIPPED DEFAULT dip-buy feature vs a flat fixed-schedule baseline, across 3 non-overlapping windows x 8 symbols, same anchors as candle-strategy research: train=2026-03-14..2026-06-12 (win 6/8 symbols, +0.26pp ROI), test=2026-06-12..2026-08-11 (win 2/8, -0.07pp ROI, essentially noise), plus a 3rd older window 2025-12-15..2026-03-14 (win 8/8, +0.61pp ROI). Mixed across windows -- does NOT clear a majority-of-symbols win in the trending-up test window, so not a clean unconditional edge by this research programs own anti-noise standard. But mechanism is explicable (extra buys land at locally-lower 24h-dip prices by construction, so it can only help when dips occur and is a no-op, not a loss, when they dont) -- consistent with 2/3 windows meaningfully positive and the 3rd being near-zero rather than negative. Already the shipped default; this run VALIDATES keeping it as-is, does not argue for a change either direction.

More aggressive dip-buy variant (threshold 5%->3%, multiplier 1.5x->2.5x) vs the shipped default, same 3-window DCA ROI methodology (see sibling entry). Beats shipped default on ROI in older window (8/8 symbols, +1.72pp) and train window (7/8, +0.55pp) but only 4/8 (50%, +0.09pp, noise-level) in the trending-up test window -- not a clean 3/3-window win. Also deploys 13-30% MORE total capital than the default across symbols (more dip events trigger at the lower threshold) -- a real practical capital/liquidity requirement and larger concentration of exposure into still-declining assets, not free even though the per-dollar ROI compares fairly. Given the borderline test-window result and the added capital/risk footprint, NOT adopted as new default -- would need a cleaner win in a genuinely trending-up window before justifying more aggressive dip-buying as the shipped default.
